prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key proposals (2001)

- Constitutional and governance: Seek an independence referendum via a majority of Scottish MPs; expand powers of the Scottish Parliament. Create a written constitution; inclusive citizenship rules; retain the monarch as head of state subject to referendum. Introduce proportional representation for all levels. Cut and democratise quangos; enhance civil service opportunities.

- Public finance and investment: Create a sovereign-style fund (Scottish Fund for Future Generations) from surplus oil revenues to finance services sustainably. Establish a not‑for‑profit Scottish Trust for Public Investment (STPI) to cut infrastructure financing costs versus PFI/PPP.

- Taxation: No rise in overall tax burden without mandate. Launch a comprehensive review for fairness and simplicity, aiming to reduce business taxes. Immediately cut fuel duty by 10p per gallon, funded by a new 5p income tax band on earnings over £100,000.

- Education and children: Abolish tuition fees; rebuild maintenance grants as resources allow. Lower voting age to 16; implement UNCRC; create a Children’s Commissioner. Establish an Education Convention; reduce P1–P3 class sizes to 18 (starting in deprived areas); end league tables; reduce assessment burdens; major school refurbishment via STPI. Support Gaelic-medium education where demand exists; anti-racism measures; inclusive education; support for Catholic schools’ needs.

- Jobs and enterprise: Infrastructure investment, universal broadband, reskilling agenda, streamlined development agencies. Reorient tourism bodies to global marketing and improve access. Devolve and refocus employment programmes.

- Pay and labour rights: Raise minimum wage to £4.36 for all ages; end age differentials; consider relief for small firms. Enact a statutory Charter of Trade Union Rights; support EU worker involvement rules.

- Health and care: Create a National Health Care Commission to set strategy and end “postcode” treatment; make Health Technology Board decisions binding and expand its budget. Free fruit in primary schools and nutritional standards for school meals. Reintroduce free dental check‑ups; freeze and review prescription charges. Invest in equipment and staffing (at least 1,500 more nurses), halve inpatient waiting times, fund hospital cleanliness, and provide free personal care for older people.

- Environment, energy, water: National Environment Plan with climate targets; 12% of energy (25% electricity) from renewables by 2010; no new nuclear, focus on decommissioning expertise. Promote resource efficiency and polluter‑pays. Review water industry finances, cap charge hikes, halt privatisation by stealth, democratise governance.

- Transport: Use STPI to finance rail electrification and reopenings (e.g., Borders line, airport links), road maintenance and targeted upgrades (e.g., M74 extension, A9), light rail in cities, a national concessions scheme, a “public share” in Railtrack, public control of air traffic control. Reduce ferry fares (pilot Road Equivalent Tariffs) and abolish Skye Bridge tolls; expand direct flights.

- Rural, agriculture, fisheries, land: Small business rates relief; lower rural fuel costs; improve transport; protect core services. Post–foot-and-mouth review (imports, labelling, local abattoirs). Avoid early “gold‑plating” of EU rules; support diversification (organic/free‑range); mitigate Less Favoured Areas impacts. Compensated tie‑ups, technical conservation, decentralised fisheries management; bolster processing and aquaculture; independent inquiry into salmon farming; enhance SEPA resources. Expand community land rights and involvement; national freshwater fisheries policy.

- Housing and communities: Seek UK assumption of historic council housing debt; devolve housing benefit; invest via STPI; oppose wholesale stock transfer; “Tenants First” principle. End competitive “challenge” funding for the voluntary sector; provide multi‑year core funding; exempt from water charges. Tackle rough sleeping and hidden homelessness.

- Social justice, security, pensions: National anti‑poverty strategy and “poverty proofing”; fair, fast asylum assessment and end vouchers. Restore earnings link for the basic pension using NI surplus; address MIG distortions; spread winter fuel support weekly; consider extension to severely disabled under 60. Streamline benefits delivery into a single agency; simplify housing benefit; improve disability and carer support; review Working Families Tax Credit disincentives and uptake.

- Justice and policing: Fund 1,000 additional police officers; parental compensation orders for youth damage; lifetime supervision for high‑risk offenders; implement serious offender recommendations; establish a Sentencing Advisory Panel; speed up lower‑court cases; retain more fines in Scotland; expand drug courts and rehabilitation.

- Europe, international, defence, culture, media, sport: Support EU membership with subsidiarity and referendums on major transfers; possible euro entry subject to conditions and consent. Remove nuclear weapons, oppose missile defence, phase out NATO membership while maintaining cooperation; create a professional Scottish Defence Force. Focus overseas representation on trade, investment and tourism; raise aid to UN target, untie aid, create a coordinating “Aid from Scotland.” Reform arts funding (including a national theatre), boost traditional arts, start a Scottish Lottery; strengthen Gaelic and Scots. Expand digital broadcasting powers and Scottish scheduling; support a national “Scottish Six.” Prioritise community sport, football academies, and a major tournament bid.
